material_suggestions.notes: easy to machine and lighter than iron; increase wall thickness for stiffness
better heat and creep resistance than PLA; use generous walls and metal inserts
acceptable for fit checks; avoid sustained load or high temperature

parts.name: Compact no-flicker pillow block bearing housing
main_features: low footed mounting base with two raised foot pads
solid central pedestal/saddle body under the bearing
rounded horizontal bearing boss blended into the pedestal
thin subtractive cap split-line groove, no solid top slab
two symmetric oval foot mounting slots or holes
compact UCP-style cast housing silhouette without tall arch ribs

usage.label: How and where the part will be used

boss_diameter.note: keeps radial support around the bearing

edge_margin.note: minimum bolt-hole center distance from free edge

fit_guidance_mm.mounting_hole_clearance: M5 clearance = 5.5 mm, M6 clearance = 6.6 mm

design_rules: A true pillow block is not a hollow ring on a flat plate; it needs a compact pedestal/saddle body that supports the bearing boss from below.
Match a UCP-style pillow block: two low feet, solid center pedestal, rounded bearing body, horizontal shaft axis, and a thin subtractive cap split-line groove.
Do not generate tall external arch ribs, bridge frames, or large triangular side frames around the bearing.
Do not add a solid rectangular top slab, roof, cap block, or bridge over the bearing; the upper body should remain rounded/compact.
The bearing boss must be blended into a solid base pedestal so it reads as a cast mounted bearing housing.
The bearing seat, shaft bore, and mounting holes must be subtracted after the solid body union.
The shaft bore and bearing seat must be coaxial and horizontal for a pillow block.
The base must include two symmetric foot mounting holes or oval mounting slots with realistic edge distance.
Wall thickness around the bearing seat should be at least 4 mm, preferably 6-10 mm for printed parts.
Ask for usage before choosing material and duty class.
validation_criteria: Defines shaft_diameter, bearing_od, bearing_width, wall_thickness, base_thickness, and mount_hole_diameter.
Uses difference() for bearing seat, shaft bore, and mounting holes.
Uses a for-loop or symmetric placements for repeated foot mounting holes or slots.
Includes low base and foot pads wider than the bearing boss.
Includes solid pedestal/saddle/body geometry below the boss.
Bearing boss is rounded and blended into the pedestal, not floating above it.
Avoids the failure mode of only a circular tube/ring sitting on a flat rectangular plate.
Avoids solid rectangular top slabs, roofs, or cap blocks above the rounded housing.
Avoids tall arch bridge frames and large external triangular ribs.
failure_modes: Tube or hollow ring sitting on a flat plate with no pedestal support.
Tall arch or bridge frame around the bearing instead of a compact cast housing.
Massive rectangular top slab or roof over the bearing boss.
Bearing seat added as a solid cylinder instead of subtracted.
Shaft bore not aligned with bearing axis.
Single center mounting hole instead of paired foot holes or slots.
Wall thickness too thin around the bearing seat.
No usage information, leading to weak material choice.

material_suggestions.use_case: industrial static mounts and damped machine supports

material_suggestions.notes: good machinability; increase boss wall thickness
use heat-set inserts and generous walls

footed_base.purpose: Carries bolt loads and gives the housing stable mounting feet.
footed_base.openscad_snippet: translate([0,0,base_thickness/2]) cube([base_length, base_width, base_thickness], center=true); for (x=[-mount_hole_spacing/2,mount_hole_spacing/2]) translate([x,0,base_thickness+foot_pad_thickness/2]) cube([foot_pad_length, foot_pad_width, foot_pad_thickness], center=true);

pedestal_saddle.purpose: Creates the compact solid body below the bearing boss, matching a UCP-style cast pillow block.
pedestal_saddle.openscad_snippet: translate([0,0,base_thickness+pedestal_height/2]) cube([pedestal_width, pedestal_depth, pedestal_height], center=true); hull(){ translate([0,0,base_thickness+8]) cube([pedestal_width+8,pedestal_depth,10], center=true); translate([0,0,boss_center_z]) rotate([90,0,0]) cylinder(h=boss_width,d=boss_diameter,center=true); }

horizontal_bearing_boss.purpose: Provides radial wall around the bearing seat on a horizontal shaft axis.

bearing_seat_cut.purpose: Creates the bearing pocket as a subtraction, not a solid insert.

shaft_bore_cut.purpose: Creates coaxial shaft clearance through the bearing axis.

paired_foot_mount_holes.purpose: Creates two symmetric oval foot mounting slots with realistic edge distance.
paired_foot_mount_holes.openscad_snippet: for (x=[-mount_hole_spacing/2, mount_hole_spacing/2]) translate([x,0,base_thickness/2]) rounded_slot(slot_length, mount_hole_diameter, base_thickness+foot_pad_thickness+8);

cap_split_or_ribs.purpose: Adds a thin subtractive cap split groove; never add a solid top slab, roof, or bridge block.
constraints: include split/cap/rib/web cue for pillow block designs

constraint_checks.expression: bearing_seat_cut appears inside difference() after union()
constraint_checks.message: Bearing seat must be removed from the solid housing body.

constraint_checks.expression: shaft bore transform equals bearing seat transform
constraint_checks.message: Shaft bore and bearing seat must share the same horizontal axis.
A true pillow block needs support below the boss, not just a ring on a plate.

constraint_checks.expression: two symmetric foot holes generated from mount_hole_spacing
constraint_checks.message: Use two base holes for a pillow block foot.
Mounting holes need enough material to the base edge.

parts.name: Transmission shaft housing
design_rules: Use the simple central cylindrical housing pattern when the user asks for this transmission shaft housing form.
Create the solid housing as a union of the lower base cylinder and the central cylinder housing.
Subtract two bearing seat cavities at the derived bearing positions.
Subtract the shaft bore after the solid housing union.
Do not add extra mounting slots, raised pillow-block bosses, bridge webs, ribs, cap split grooves, or gear features unless the user explicitly asks for them.
Do not assign geometry to variables. OpenSCAD geometry statements cannot be stored in variables.
Do not declare string metadata variables such as manufacturing = "fdm" in OpenSCAD code.
failure_modes: extra pillow-block features added when the user asked for the simple cylindrical transmission shaft housing
mounting slots, ribs, bridge webs, or cap grooves added without being requested
bearing seats not subtracted from the housing body
shaft bore missing from the housing body
geometry assigned to variables instead of emitted directly in modules

parts.name: Square flanged bearing housing for 6204 bearing

usage.label: wall, plate, or frame mounting use case

design_rules: Use four symmetric corner mounting holes.
Keep the shaft axis perpendicular to the mounting flange.
Use a raised boss or thickened center around the bearing seat.
Ask for usage to choose cast iron, steel, aluminum, or printed polymer.
validation_criteria: Central bore and bearing seat are coaxial.
Flange size is larger than boss diameter and hole pattern.
failure_modes: Only two holes on a square flange.
Shaft axis parallel to flange when perpendicular was required.
Insufficient material between bearing seat and bolt holes.

material_suggestions.notes: good for robotics and test fixtures

parts.name: Take-up bearing housing with slotted adjustment base
standards: belt and chain tensioning mounted bearing practice

usage.label: belt, chain, or roller tensioning use case

slot_radius.note: rounded ends of the adjustment slots

design_rules: Use rounded-end slots, not simple rectangular cuts.
Slot direction should match the adjustment direction.
Keep boss and shaft axis aligned while base slots are offset symmetrically.
validation_criteria: Slots are subtractive and have rounded ends.
Base length is greater than slot length plus edge margins.
Bearing seat and shaft bore remain coaxial.
failure_modes: Slots too close to base edge.
Rectangular slots with sharp stress raisers.
Adjustment slot direction not aligned with stated usage.

material_suggestions.use_case: belt or chain tensioner under shock load

rounded_adjustment_slots.purpose: Creates low-stress rounded-end slots instead of sharp rectangles.

constraints: bearing seat and shaft bore must share the same axis

constraint_checks.expression: slots are generated with hull() of two cylinders
constraint_checks.message: Take-up slots need rounded ends to avoid sharp stress raisers.
Slots must not break out near the base edge.
